result.summary: Classifies the assumeutxo snapshot base block as belonging to the normal blockfile range rather than the assumed snapshot range. It adjusts blockfile flushing, block index loading, and database verification to properly handle when the snapshot base block is already present on disk before snapshot activation. It also adds functional tests covering node restarts and background validation completion in this scenario.
result.problem: If a node receives and stores the snapshot base block before loadtxoutset runs (such as via submitblock), the block is written to the normal blockfile cursor, but subsequent snapshot activation reclassifies the height as ASSUMED. This causes an assertion abort in WriteBlockUndo when the background chainstate connects the base block, or causes VerifyDB upon restart to attempt disconnecting the base block without undo data and fail startup with a false database corruption error requiring a reindex.
evidence: PR description reproduces an abort during background validation: 'node/blockstorage.cpp:985 bool node::BlockManager::WriteBlockUndo(const CBlockUndo &, BlockValidationState &, CBlockIndex &): Assertion `m_blockfile_cursors[type]` failed.'

PR description reproduces node refusing to start on restart: '[VerifyDB] Verification error: irrecoverable inconsistency in block data at 299 Corrupted block database detected. Please restart with -reindex or -reindex-chainstate to recover.'
PR author notes that 'The block database is not corrupt, so the reindex that message asks for is wasted work.'
result.card: Classifies the assumeutxo snapshot base block in the normal blockfile range instead of the assumed snapshot range, and prevents VerifyDB from attempting to disconnect it on a snapshot chainstate. Storing the snapshot base block on disk before calling loadtxoutset currently leaves the node in an unrecoverable state, aborting with an assertion failure in WriteBlockUndo during background validation or failing startup with a false database corruption error during VerifyDB. The PR description reproduces both failure modes with log output and adds functional test coverage verifying node recovery and background validation completion.
